title: Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK, consolidate tracing hooks, and modernize metrics/logging
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Remove long-standing fragilities in our observability stack by upgrading OpenTelemetry SDKs across services, retiring custom tracing wrappers, migrating metrics instrumentation to the consolidated metrics library, and switching to structured, contextual logging. Motivation: recurring incidents where traces were incomplete due to hook ordering, stale OTEL exporters, and high Cardinality metrics causing Prometheus ingestion issues. Goal is to reduce tracer loss, cut metric churn, and unlock improved latency correlation for runtime regressions. This ticket covers cross-service library upgrades, CI linting checks for instrumentation, a migration shim for legacy hooks, and a staged rollout with realtime validation dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: All backend services compiled/packaged with OpenTelemetry SDK >= 1.20 and language-specific api stable versions
Custom tracing middleware removed or wrapped by a documented shim; no service depends on deprecated trace hook API
No increase in 95th and 99th percentile request latency after upgrade (baseline comparison)
Metric cardinality reduced for high-cardinality labels flagged in the audit (see links), and Prometheus scrape stability improved
New logging format implemented for server-side services (structured JSON with trace/span ids) and validated by logging QA
CI check added to flag use of deprecated tracing APIs and unbounded label cardinality
Rollout executed to canary pool and fallback policy proven via automated rollback in <15 minutes
technical_notes: Primary languages: Go services use go.opentelemetry.io/otel; Python workers use opentelemetry-sdk package. Upgrade targets: Go to v1.19 -> v1.21, Python to 1.15 -> 1.20 depending on language compatibility tests
Problem root cause: our tracing hook insertion relied on startup ordering and a custom global tracer shim that bypassed context propagation in goroutines and background threads
Metrics change: migrate from prometheus_client custom collectors to OTLP metrics export with Prometheus receiver and implement cardinality guard rails (allowed label sets)
Logging: introduce structured logging wrapper (logfmt -> JSON) that injects trace_id and span_id into every log entry; update log ingestion parser rules accordingly
Telemetry exporters: default to OTLP/gRPC to our gateway with TLS + auth; keep a temporary sidecar to send to legacy exporters for 2 weeks
Compatibility shim: provide otel-compat package that implements legacy tracing hook functions by delegating into new API for a transitional period
Perf consideration: enable SDK batching and optimize batch sizes for high-throughput services to avoid added tail latencies
Known risk: Python worker restart behavior with SDK shutdown hook may delay process exit; implement timeout and forced flush
migration_plan: Stage 1: Create otel-compat shim repo and unit tests; land in mono-repo and update internal modules to reference shim
Stage 2: Upgrade dependency in single low-traffic service (ingest-worker-alpha) and validate end-to-end traces and metrics in staging
Stage 3: Run canary in production (5% traffic) for 48 hours with synthetic traffic replay and SLO checks
Stage 4: Gradually increase rollout to 25% then 100% while monitoring trace completeness and Prometheus scrape errors
Stage 5: Remove shim and deprecated API usages after 2 weeks of stable signals and flip CI checks to error for deprecated APIs
testing_plan: Unit tests for otel-compat shim and instrumentation adapters
Integration tests that assert trace context propagation across async boundaries and across language boundaries (Go -> Python RPC) using tracer test harness
Load test with 10k concurrent simulated requests to measure opentelemetry batching behavior and memory footprint
Prometheus scrape test: ingest synthetic metrics with high cardinality labels and verify cardinality rejection logic
End-to-end smoke: verify logs contain trace_id/span_id for a set of sample transactions and that those correlate with traces in the UI
rollout_plan: Canary deploy to cluster 'us-west-canary' for ingest and edge services
Monitor Dashboards: trace-loss ratio, span count per request, exporter errors, Prometheus scrape failures, latency p50/p95/p99
Automatic rollback if trace-loss ratio > 1.5x baseline or exporter error rate increases > 0.5% over 15m
Post-rollout: 72-hour monitoring window before deprecating legacy exporters
Communicate to SRE and platform channels before each stage; schedule 30-minute post-deploy review
